A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RM-NLHF research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original proxy-evaluation, reward-model training, benchmark, ablation, and downstream results in Sections 2–4 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds downstream reinforcement-learning outcomes in Table 4 and response-length measurements in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The RM-NLHF rewards, MetaRM architecture, losses, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Section 4.4 adds a downstream adaptation that converts pairwise judgments into pointwise rewards through Double-Elimination Tournament for policy training; v1 used tournaments for response selection.

E1.justification: Dataset and substantive task coverage remain unchanged. The new RL experiment reuses HelpSteer3 prompts and Arena-Hard-V2.0 instruction-following evaluation; it changes the training and evaluation procedure within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Existing baseline memberships are retained. The new downstream experiment compares RM-NLHF with the existing Outcome-Only approach. Its four judge models are evaluators, and newly cited reward-modeling papers are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: New Section 4.4 adds direct policy-training evaluation: DeepSeek-Distilled-Qwen-7B undergoes 100 GRPO steps on HelpSteer3 prompts using either reward model, followed by Arena-Hard-V2.0 evaluation with four judges. This substantially extends the evaluation design beyond v1's downstream BoN and Feedback-Edit protocols, which are retained.

E4.justification: New Figure 7 compares response-length trajectories during downstream RL to investigate verbosity as an explanation for performance. Existing reward-design ablations, MetaRM analyses, reward-hacking observations, and linguistic analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new judge averages and mean-response-length curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds direct downstream RL results: Table 4 reports average win rates of 52.33% for RM-NLHF and 39.41% for Outcome-Only, with 8.26% ties, across four judges. Figure 7 adds shorter-response trajectories for the RM-NLHF-trained policy. Existing numerical results remain unchanged, including v1 Table 4 retained as v2 Table 5.

T1.justification: New Appendix I introduces an idealized framework with context-dependent evaluation dimensions and nonnegative weights defining 'reward causality,' an ideal weighted reward, and formulations for BT, conditional BT, and critique/label supervision in Equations 9–13. This substantially expands the formal modeling content, although no theorems or proofs are supplied.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a contribution claiming a theoretical account of four reward-modeling mechanisms, the necessity of the proposed approach, and remaining theory-practice gaps. The abstract, central empirical and MetaRM contributions, and conclusion otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: Appendix I substantially expands interpretation through causal alignment, automatic discovery of evaluation dimensions and weights, and claimed failure boundaries of BT and conditional reward models. Section 4.4 additionally interprets shorter training responses as evidence that downstream gains reflect quality rather than verbosity.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 specifies the new downstream experiment's policy and reward models, prompt source, 100-step budget, tournament conversion, and judge identities. Existing implementation details, hardware disclosures, hyperparameter tables, and prompts are retained; no new code or data release is announced.

R1.justification: Appendix I adds substantial positioning against traditional BT, conditional reward modeling, and outcome-supervised GRMs through a four-way taxonomy and discussion of their limitations. New references include RLBFF, ArenaRL, and work on robust reward modeling and multimodal moderation; Section 5 itself is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order remain intact. v2 inserts an RL subsection, relabels the earlier downstream section as test-time scaling, adds a contribution bullet and Appendix I, and moves the unchanged prompts to Appendix J. The affiliation changes from Tongyi Lab to Qwen-Character Team.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with clearer data-stream and outcome-reward components. v2 adds the RL comparison table, response-length plot, and theoretical summary table. Other displays retain their content and design, with localized relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Section 4.4 strengthens practical validation by testing whether the reward model improves policy training, which v1 did not evaluate directly, and reports advantages across four judges. The gain is limited by the single 100-step setting and absent uncertainty estimates. Appendix I broadens explanation and positioning, but its causal and necessity assertions lack proofs or causal tests, tempering the overall improvement.
